folder_html:
LIVE CHLOROPHYLL / ALGAL ACTIVITY

Chlorophyll-a concentration at the lake surface, a proxy for phytoplankton abundance/biomass. NOT a toxin measurement and NOT a harmful-algal-bloom diagnosis.

Chlorophyll-a concentration (mg/m^3), FIXED absolute scale LOWEST 0.001 (dark blue) → 0.01 → 0.1 → 1.0 → 10 bloom (red) → HIGHEST+ 100 (deep purple). Each half-decade owns an equal share of the color; displayed values are true concentrations, never altered. High values indicate biomass/activity, not toxins.

Units: mg/m^3
Source: NOAA CoastWatch S-NPP+NOAA-20 VIIRS chlorophyll-a NRT gapfilled Daily (ERDDAP nesdisVHNnoaaSNPPnoaa20NRTchlaGapfilledDaily), fallback SQ Daily (nesdisVHNSQchlaDaily)
Update: daily composites
Data time: 2026-10-04 08:00 AM EDT (7-day median mosaic)
Processed: 2026-10-05 10:56 PM EDT
Why high values turn red/purple: Fixed absolute scale with anchors where lake water lives: background water spreads blue through green, active water reads yellow-orange, and only true blooms reach red-violet/deep-purple.
Provenance: ERDDAP dataset
